title: Why the Casino Always Wins (It's Just Math) 🎰 #shorts
description:
An American roulette wheel has 38 pockets but pays only 35 to 1 on a single number. That gap is a 5.26% house edge: about $5.26 lost per $100 bet, on average.
Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, "Roulette: House odds"; PokerNews, "American vs European Roulette". Education, not financial advice.
script: A casino doesn't need luck. The math wins before the wheel even spins.
An American roulette wheel has thirty-eight pockets.
Bet on one number and win, and they pay you thirty-five to one.
But fair odds would be thirty-seven to one.
That small gap is the house edge. Five point two six percent.
So for every hundred dollars you bet, you lose about five dollars and twenty-six cents, on average.
One night, that's luck. A million spins, it's a guarantee.
In money, the math always wins. Make sure it's working for you, not against you.
